senses.gloss: The stage of a lawsuit in which each side must hand over its evidence to the other.
examples: The company turned over thousands of emails during *discovery*.
Both sides are still in *discovery*, so no trial date has been set.
Her lawyer asked for the security tapes in *discovery*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing so bad that it brings shame on others.
examples: The condition of these sidewalks is a *disgrace*.
He called the ruling a *disgrace* to the profession.
The way they treated their workers was a national *disgrace*.

senses.gloss: A restaurant worker whose job is washing dishes.
examples: He started as a *dishwasher* and worked his way up to line cook.
The diner is hiring a *dishwasher* for the night shift.
Two *dishwashers* quit the same week.

senses.gloss: A serious upheaval that disturbs the normal working of a society or an economy.
examples: The plant closing caused real economic *dislocation* in the county.
The war brought years of social *dislocation*.
Automation is creating *dislocations* across the job market.

senses.gloss: A refusal to take an idea, a person, or a complaint seriously.
examples: Her casual *dismissal* of their concerns only made things worse.
The mayor's *dismissal* of the report angered residents.
I was surprised by his quick *dismissal* of such a promising idea.

senses.gloss: A judge's decision to throw a case out of court.
examples: Her attorney filed a motion for *dismissal*.
The judge granted a *dismissal* of all charges.
The company is hoping for an early *dismissal* of the lawsuit.

senses.gloss: A confused or untidy state; a lack of order.
examples: The apartment was in complete *disorder* after the move.
Papers lay in *disorder* all across the desk.
The retreating troops fell back in *disorder*.

senses.gloss: Violent or unruly behavior by a crowd.
examples: Police were called in after a night of *disorder* downtown.
The new rules are meant to prevent *disorder* at the stadium.
The city saw three days of *disorder* following the verdict.

senses.gloss: The act of sending someone or something off to a destination.
examples: The governor ordered the *dispatch* of the National Guard.
We got an email confirming the *dispatch* of our order.
The *dispatch* of relief supplies began the next morning.

senses.gloss: The office or crew that sends out police, fire, and ambulance units by radio.
examples: *Dispatch* says the ambulance is four minutes out.
She works nights in *dispatch* at the sheriff's office.
Call it in to *dispatch* before you go inside.

senses.gloss: The grinder in a kitchen sink drain that chops up food waste.
examples: Don't put coffee grounds down the *disposal*.
The *disposal* is jammed again.
Run cold water while the *disposal* is going.

senses.gloss: Coolness or a lack of warmth between people.
examples: There's been a *distance* between the brothers ever since the funeral.
She kept a certain *distance* from her coworkers.
You could hear the *distance* in his voice.

senses.gloss: Special honor, or excellence that sets someone apart.
examples: She graduated with *distinction*.
He's a scientist of real *distinction*.
Her grandfather served with *distinction* in the Navy.

senses.gloss: Great mental pain, worry, or sorrow.
examples: She sued the company for emotional *distress*.
The fireworks caused the dogs obvious *distress*.
He hid his *distress* well, but his hands were shaking.

senses.gloss: The way something is spread out across an area or a group.
examples: The map shows the *distribution* of oak trees across the state.
Economists argue about the *distribution* of income.
The test scores followed a normal *distribution*.

senses.gloss: A part of a city known for a particular business or character.
examples: We had dinner in the theater *district*.
Old warehouses in the arts *district* have been turned into lofts.
The financial *district* empties out on weekends.

senses.gloss: An enjoyable activity that takes your mind off things.
examples: Crossword puzzles are her favorite evening *diversion*.
The county fair was a welcome *diversion* after a hard summer.
He took up woodworking as a *diversion*.

senses.gloss: The redirecting of money, water, or traffic to another use or route.
examples: Auditors uncovered the *diversion* of grant money into private accounts.
The dam allows the *diversion* of river water to farms.
A *diversion* of northbound traffic sent us onto side streets.

senses.gloss: A benefit that comes later from something you did earlier.
examples: The extra hours of practice paid *dividends* in the playoffs.
Learning a second language pays *dividends* for the rest of your life.
The cleanup brought an unexpected *dividend*: the tourists came back.

senses.gloss: The arithmetic operation of finding how many times one number goes into another.
examples: Third graders start long *division* this year.
She's fine at multiplication but still struggles with *division*.
Use *division* to find the average.

senses.gloss: The act of splitting something into parts or sharing it out.
examples: The will spells out the *division* of the property.
They argued for months over the *division* of assets.
The *division* of labor in that kitchen was never fair.

senses.gloss: A serious disagreement that splits a group into opposing sides.
examples: The vote exposed deep *divisions* within the party.
There's a growing *division* between the older and younger members.
The issue created *divisions* that never healed.

senses.gloss: A large section of a company or organization.
examples: She runs the company's Latin American *division*.
The consumer products *division* had a strong quarter.
Two *divisions* were merged to cut costs.

senses.gloss: A bandage or pad placed over a wound.
examples: The nurse changed the *dressing* on his leg twice a day.
Keep the *dressing* dry until Friday.
She packed gauze and sterile *dressings* in the first-aid kit.

senses.gloss: A seasoned bread mixture baked in a pan and served with turkey.
examples: Grandma makes cornbread *dressing* every Thanksgiving.
Save room for the turkey and *dressing*.
In our family the *dressing* is baked in a pan, not in the bird.

senses.gloss: A network of connected companies, products, or people that depend on one another.
examples: Once you buy the phone, you're inside their whole *ecosystem*.
The city has built a real startup *ecosystem*.
Outside developers are the heart of the *ecosystem*.

senses.gloss: The quality of doing a job well without wasting time, money, or effort.
examples: The new software improved the office's *efficiency*.
He runs the warehouse with impressive *efficiency*.
They cut costs by finding *efficiencies* in shipping.

senses.gloss: A small apartment in which one room serves as living room, bedroom, and kitchen.
examples: She rented an *efficiency* near campus.
The building has six *efficiencies* on the top floor.
It's only an *efficiency*, but the rent is cheap.

senses.gloss: The permanent removal of unwanted hair with a fine electric needle.
examples: She had *electrolysis* done on her upper lip.
The spa offers waxing, laser, and *electrolysis*.
*Electrolysis* takes several sessions to finish.

senses.gloss: The raising of someone to a higher rank or position.
examples: His *elevation* to the Supreme Court took months of hearings.
Her *elevation* to partner surprised no one.
The *elevation* of a new archbishop drew a big crowd.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that makes others feel ashamed.
examples: The whole episode was an *embarrassment* to the department.
He's become an *embarrassment* to his own family.
The misspelled sign was a small *embarrassment* for the school.
